summary.text: 服 commonly means ‘clothes’ or ‘wear’; it also has uses meaning ‘subdue’ or ‘submit’. A proposed account analyzes it as a later compound related to 𠬝, while another sees a person serving at a tray. The added element’s identity and contribution remain disputed.

formation.text: The leading analysis is phonosemantic: 𠬝 provides a sound cue, and an added element may contribute meaning. The proposed added element is variously identified as 凡, 舟, or a tray-like shape; a competing analysis sees a person presenting a tray. The compound analysis is probable, but the element’s identity and meaning are unsettled.

components.text: 𠬝 is analyzed as a graph combining 又, interpreted as a hand, and 卩, interpreted as a kneeling person, to depict subduing. In 服 it is proposed as the phonetic component; the cited Old Chinese reconstruction gives both graphs the same form. The proposed pictorial analysis concerns 𠬝 itself, not its role in 服.

sound_limitation.text: The sound match supports a phonetic role in this proposed compound, but does not independently establish that 𠬝 meant ‘subdue’ in every early occurrence.

sound.text: The Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction gives 𠬝 ‘subdue; submit’ and 服 ‘garment; wear’ and ‘subdue; submit’ the same form, supporting 𠬝 as a sound cue in this proposed compound.

components.text: The added shape is identified in competing accounts as 凡 ‘tray’, 舟, or a tray-like form. One account proposes a change from a 凡-like form to 舟 and later to the modern 月-like shape; the exact forms and sequence are disputed. Another analysis treats the whole graph as a person serving at a tray. The element’s semantic contribution is not settled.

history.text: The selected oracle-style and bronze-style images are modern redraws labeled as forms of 服. They represent candidate historical forms, but their labels do not establish a reading or an evolutionary sequence; the bronze-style form does not resolve whether the disputed element is 凡, 舟, or tray-like.

The transmitted Shuowen explains 服 as 用也, gives a vehicle-related alternative, and analyzes the graph as 从舟𠬝聲. It also records an old form 𦨈; a later commentary disputes 舟 in the vehicle explanation. These are historical lexicographic accounts, not independent confirmation of the graph’s earliest construction.

Early uses reported for 服 include an oracle-bone place name and a bronze inscription use for office or duty. The cited 班簋 inscription occurs in a context interpreted as succession to duties; these uses do not by themselves establish the graph’s origin or a path to the clothing sense.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic analysis related to 𠬝 competes with an interpretation of a person serving at a tray. The identity of the added element and the exact graphic transitions remain disputed.
A quiver or arrow-case sense is attested in 箕服, but its relation to other uses is unresolved: it may be a separate word, a semantic development, or a use of the graph for another word.

senses.period: oracle-bone use reported; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: An analysis of 𠬝 reports an oracle-bone verb meaning ‘conquer’ and a noun for conquered people. The reading and interpretation of individual occurrences are not uncontested.
服 is reported in a bronze inscription in a context interpreted as succession to office or duties. The evidence does not establish a development from ‘subdue’.

senses.period: classical textual attestations; manuscript dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted classical quotations attest 服 meaning ‘wear’ and ‘clothing’. Their historical relation to ‘subdue’ or ‘office’ is not established.

senses.period: historical use in a compound; earliest date unresolved
senses.text: 箕服 is attested with the meaning ‘arrow case’ or ‘quiver’. Whether this reflects a distinct word, a semantic development, or graph borrowing is unresolved.

limitations.text: The listed senses do not establish a chronology or semantic chain. In particular, no supported transition links ‘subdue’ or ‘office’ to ‘clothing’, and the status of the quiver use remains unclear.

overview.text: 服 commonly means ‘clothes’ or ‘wear’; it can also mean ‘subdue’ or ‘submit’. One proposed analysis links it to 𠬝 as a sound cue, with an added element whose identity and meaning remain disputed.

components.text: 𠬝 is analyzed as depicting subduing and is proposed as the sound cue in 服.
The added shape is identified variously as 凡, 舟, or a tray; its history and contribution remain disputed.

relationships.text: In the proposed compound analysis, 𠬝 supplies a sound cue for 服; the cited Old Chinese reconstruction gives them matching forms.
One analysis identifies the added element as 舟, following the transmitted Shuowen account; other accounts identify a tray-like form or 凡. Its semantic contribution is unsettled.
One proposed graphic history treats 服 as a later expanded form associated with the earlier graph 𠬝.
